To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) design is a creative and constructive process where new objects are created and (2) the creative process is not a mere combination of already existing objects but rather the expansion of both new propositions and new objects by means of free choices.

(i) design is an imaginative constructivist activity, (ii) the notion of imagination is essential to understand design and its creative aspects, and (iii) imagination can be interpreted as an extension of constructivist processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is constructivism in design?
the identification and integration of a new type of constructivism in the design research field that we call imaginative constructivism.
a theoretical analysis of constructivism in order to provide new insights into the nature of design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
design is an imaginative constructivist activity, where new objects are not only a bottom-up combination of known objects but can also be the result of creative free choices of a subject.
constructivism is a foundational issue of design and that a form of imagination plays a key role in this respect.

the notion of constructivist process in design is a multifaceted notion, where different forms of constructivism need to be identified, and the notion of imagination needs to be considered as a central issue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided the foundations of a theory of imaginative design, where the designer is a creative subject that can make free choices in the course of the design process, and the design process is a process that allows the expansion of propositions, representations and objects.
design is an imaginative constructivist activity, where the designer’s creative acts play a key role in constructing new objects, propositions and representations.
the creative and constructive nature of design is not a matter of choice but a foundational issue that needs to be addressed by design research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consideration of creative aspects in design processes can be fruitfully grounded on a constructivist approach.

a more complete picture of design as an imaginative constructivist activity needs to take into account the creative aspects of the activity, which are not considered by the existing paradigms of constructivism in other fields.
a new form of constructivist design needs to be explored, where the creative act is not only a part of design, but also an essential feature of design itself.
